spots.name: Umayyad Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Umayyad Mosque, also known as the Great Mosque of Damascus, located in the old city of Damascus, the capital of Syria, is one of the largest and oldest mosques in the world. It is considered to be the oldest mosque still in use in its original form.

spots.name: Mausoleum of Saladin
spots.summary: The Mausoleum of Saladin holds the resting place and grave of the medieval Muslim Ayyubid Sultan Saladin. It is adjacent to the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus, Syria. It was built in 1196, three years after the death of Saladin.

names.ja: サラーフッディーン廟

spots.name: Old city of Damascus
spots.summary: The old city of Damascus is the historic city centre of Damascus, Syria. The old city, which is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, contains numerous archaeological sites, including some historical churches and mosques.

spots.name: Al-Azm Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al-Azm Palace is a palace in Damascus, Syria, built in 1749. Located north of Al-Buzuriyah Souq in the Ancient City of Damascus, the palace was built in 1749 to be the private residence for As'ad Pasha al-Azm, the governor of Damascus; during the French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon, it housed the French Institute.

spots.name: Sulaymaniyya Takiyya

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sulaymaniyya Takiyya is a takiyya, located in Damascus, Syria, on the right bank of the Barada River. Commissioned by the Ottoman sultan Suleiman the Magnificent, the western building of the complex was built, following the plans of Mimar Sinan, between 1554 and 1559.

names.ja: テッキーヤ・スレイマニエ・ジャーミイ

spots.name: Bab Tuma
spots.summary: Bab Tuma is a neighborhood located in the old city of Damascus in Syria. It is named after one of the seven gates of old city of Damascus, located within the neighbourhood.

spots.name: Citadel of Damascus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Citadel of Damascus is an Ayyubid-era medieval fortified palace and citadel in Damascus, Syria. It is part of the Ancient City of Damascus, which was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979.

spots.name: Khan As'ad Pasha

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Khan As'ad Pasha is the largest caravanserai in the Old City of Damascus, covering an area of 2,500 square metres (27,000 sq ft). Situated along Al-Buzuriyah Souq, it was built and named after As'ad Pasha al-Azm, the governor of Damascus, in 1751–52.

spots.name: Straight Street
spots.summary: Straight Street is the old decumanus maximus, the main east–west Roman road, of Damascus, Syria. It runs from east to west through the old city. It was originally built during the Seleucid period.

spots.name: Mariamite Cathedral of Damascus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mariamite Cathedral of Damascus, also known as the Maryamiyya Church, is one of the oldest Greek Orthodox churches in Damascus, Syria and holds the seat of the Greek Orthodox Church of Antioch. The church complex is located on the Street Called Straight.

spots.name: National Museum of Damascus

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Museum of Damascus is a museum in the heart of Damascus, Syria. As the country's national museum as well as its largest, this museum covers the entire range of Syrian history spanning over 11 millennia.

names.ja: ダマスクス国立博物館

spots.name: Khadra Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Khadra Palace, known in Arabic as Qubbat al-Khadra, was a residence of the Umayyad caliphs in Damascus. It was founded by the first Umayyad caliph, Mu'awiya I, while he was governor of Syria under Caliph Uthman.

spots.name: Cathedral of Our Lady of the Dormition

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of Our Lady of the Dormition, also known as The Olive Church or the Melkite Greek Catholic Patriarchal Cathedral of the Dormition of Our Lady, is the cathedral of the Melkite Greek Catholic Church in the city of Damascus, Syria.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of Our Lady of the Dormition

names.es: Catedral de Nuestra Señora de la Dormición

spots.name: Statue of Saladin
spots.summary: The Statue of Saladin is an oversize equestrian bronze statue depicting the Ayyubid Sultan Saladin located in front of the 11th century Citadel of Damascus, in the Ancient City of Damascus in Damascus, Syria. The statue was designed by Syrian sculptor Abdallah al-Sayed.

spots.name: Umayyad Square
spots.summary: Umayyad Square is a large and important square in Damascus, Syria. It connects the city center with several important highways and areas, and contains important buildings, including the Ministry of Defense, Syria's national Opera House and the headquarters of the Syrian Armed Forces.

spots.name: Bab Sharqi
spots.summary: Bab Sharqi, also known as the Gate of the Sun, is one of the seven ancient city gates of Damascus, Syria. Its modern name comes from its location in the eastern side of the city.

names.ja: ダマスクス旧市街の東門

spots.name: Sayyida Ruqayya Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sayyida Ruqayya Mosque is a Shia mosque and mausoleum complex, located in Damascus, Syria. The complex contains the grave of Ruqayya bint Husayn, the young daughter of Husayn. It is a holy site in Shia Islam.

spots.name: Nur al-Din Madrasa
spots.summary: The Nur al-Din Madrasa is a funerary madrasa in Damascus, Syria. It is in the Suq al-Khayattin, inside the city walls. It was built in 1167 by Nūr ad-Dīn Zangī, atabeg of Syria, who is buried there. The complex includes a mosque, a madrasa, and the mausoleum of the founder.

names.ja: ヌールッディーン・マドラサ

spots.name: Temple of Jupiter, Damascus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Temple of Jupiter in Damascus was built by the Romans, beginning during the rule of Augustus in the first century AD and with further works occurring at various times up until the rule of Constantius II.

names.ja: ダマスクスのユピテル神殿

spots.name: Al-Adiliyah Madrasa
spots.summary: Al-Adiliyah Madrasa is a 13th-century madrasa located in Damascus, Syria. it was founded by the Ayyubid Sultan Al-Adil I in 1215.

names.ja: アーディリーヤ・マドラサ

spots.name: Syriac Catholic cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Syriac Catholic Cathedral of Saint Paul is the cathedral of the Syriac Catholic Church, located in Damascus, Syria. It is the see of the Syriac Catholic Archeparchy of Damascus and is located in the Christian quarter of Damascus, 100 m west of Bab Sharqi.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Syriac Catholic Cathedral of Saint Paul

spots.name: Sinan Pasha Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sinan Pasha Mosque or Al-Sinaniyya Mosque is an early Ottoman-era mosque in Damascus, Syria, located along Suq Sinaniyya Street.

spots.name: Bab al-Jabiyah
spots.summary: Bab al-Jabiya is one of the seven ancient city-gates of Damascus, Syria. During the Roman era, the gate was dedicated to Mars. Bab al-Jabiya was the main entrance on the city's west side.

names.ja: バーブ・アル＝ジャービーヤ

spots.name: Midhat Pasha Souq

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Midhat Pasha Souq also called Al-Taweel Souq is a historically important souq which forms the western fraction of the Street Called Straight in Damascus, Syria.

names.ja: ミドハト・パシャ・スーク

spots.name: Darwish Pasha Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Darwish Pasha Mosque or Al-Darwishiyya Mosque is a 16th-century mosque in the Old City of Damascus, Syria. The mosque was erected in 1574 CE by Darwish Pasha, the Ottoman governor of Damascus.

spots.name: National Library of Syria

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Library of Syria is the national legal deposit and copyright library of Syria, located in the capital Damascus overlooking the Umayyad Square.

spots.name: Aqsab Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Aqsab Mosque or Al-Aqsab Mosque or Al-Qasab Mosque, also known as Al-Sadat Mosque, is an Ayyubid-era Sunni mosque and mausoleum in Damascus, Syria. The mosque is located on Suq Sarujiyya, outside the walls of the old city, near the Bab al-Salam gate.

spots.name: Bab al-Salam
spots.summary: Bab al-Salam is one of the seven ancient city-gates of Damascus, Syria. During the Roman era, it was also known as "Gate of the Moon".

spots.name: Al-Muallaq Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al-Muallaq Mosque or Muallaq Mosque is a 15th century Mamluk era mosque in Damascus, Syria, built in 1458. It lies adjacent to the Barada River.

spots.summary: The oldest ice cream parlor in the Middle East, open since 1885. They are most famous for the Booza, a pistachio-covered ice cream with an elastic texture made of mastic and sahlab.

spots.summary: A favorite with locals and tourists, and offers the Syrian classics. It is located in the courtyard of a beautiful Damascene house.
